title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (ISA) Certificate of Eligibility and Status of Residence
source: Immigration Services Agency of Japan, Ministry of Justice
publisher: Ministry of Justice, Government of Japan
content:
Foreign nationals seeking to relocate to Japan for employment, study, or long-term residence must obtain a Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) before applying for an entry visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate abroad.

The CoE is issued by regional immigration bureaus across Japan upon petition by a sponsoring employer, university, or legal guarantor. Common work visa categories include Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Highly Skilled Professional, Intra-Company Transferee, and Specified Skilled Worker.

Upon arrival at major international airports (such as Haneda, Narita, or Kansai), medium-to-long-term residents receive a Residence Card (Zairyu Card). Within 14 days of securing a permanent residence, cardholders must register their address at the local municipal or ward office.

title: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) National Health Insurance (NHI) System
source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Government of Japan
content:
Japan maintains a universal healthcare coverage system (Kokumin Kaihoken). All residents, including foreign nationals staying in Japan for more than three months, are legally mandated to enroll in public health insurance.

Employees of Japanese companies are generally enrolled in Employees' Health Insurance (Shakai Hoken) sponsored jointly by employer and employee. Self-employed individuals, students, and freelancers enroll in National Health Insurance (Kokumin Kenko Hoken) administered by municipal ward offices.

Under both systems, patients pay a co-payment of 30% of total medical costs at clinics and hospitals, while the insurance covers the remaining 70%. The High-Cost Medical Expense Benefit caps patient out-of-pocket expenses monthly based on taxable income tiers.

title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government (TMG) Resident Registration and My Number Procedures
content:
Foreign residents moving into Tokyo must visit their local special ward office (ku-yakusho) or municipal city office (shi-yakusho) within 14 days of establishing an address to complete the moving-in notification (Tennyu-todoke).

The ward office records the address onto the back of the Residence Card and enters the resident into the Basic Resident Ledger (Juminhyo). A copy of the Juminhyo is required for opening bank accounts, mobile contracts, and rental leases.

Residents also receive a 12-digit Individual Number (My Number). Residents can apply for a plastic My Number Card equipped with an IC chip, which enables digital verification, official certificate printing at convenience stores, and online administrative tax filing.

title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Disaster Prevention and Earthquake Preparedness (Bosai Portal)
source: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Disaster Prevention Division
content:
Tokyo is situated in a seismically active zone, and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government provides comprehensive disaster preparedness protocols through its official Disaster Prevention Portal.

Emergency hotlines in Japan are 110 for Police and 119 for Fire and Ambulance services (both support multilingual interpretation). In the event of a major earthquake, residents are advised to protect themselves under sturdy furniture, turn off gas valves once shaking subsides, and evacuate to designated regional evacuation areas (Kouiki Hinanbasho) if fire hazards arise.

Residents are advised to maintain emergency survival kits containing at least three days of non-perishable food, water (3 liters per person per day), flashlights, portable batteries, and personal medical documentation.
